outcome: Every account scored and tiered against your written ICP by an agent that cites its evidence, with the rationale on the CRM record

inputs.ask: Who do you sell to, and who do you refuse? Name the fit signals and, just as important, the disqualifiers
inputs.why: The criteria ARE the prompt. There are no point weights in code, so a vague ICP produces vague scores and the disqualifiers are what cap a bad account at 20.
inputs.derive: If the workspace already has closed-won and closed-lost data, extract the industry, size, geography and stack that separate won from lost accounts and propose the ICP from it rather than asking cold.
inputs.validate: the file names at least one disqualifier, not only fit signals

inputs.ask: Which language model should judge the accounts?
inputs.why: Scoring quality and per-account cost both live here.
inputs.derive: whichever LLM connector is already authenticated in the workspace

inputs.ask: Create cargo_score, cargo_tier, cargo_rationale and cargo_last_updated_at as properties on the CRM's account object
inputs.why: The play writes all four back. If they do not exist the run looks successful and the scores land nowhere, which is the failure mode that wastes a whole batch.
inputs.derive: read the CRM's account schema through the crm-sync connector and report which of the four are missing
inputs.validate: all four exist, and cargo_score plus cargo_tier are selected as columns on the accounts model so the tier segments can filter on them

inputs.ask: Which tiers do you want as segments, and at what score boundaries?
inputs.why: The agent emits A, B and C but the cookbook ships segments for A and C only. Tier B accounts land in no segment unless you add one.
inputs.validate: every tier the agent can emit is either covered by a segment or deliberately excluded

doneWhen: a test account run shows the agent's lookups in the trace, not a score guessed from the domain name
the CRM record carries a score with a rationale citing real evidence and named ICP criteria
after the next model refresh the account appears in the matching tier segment

cost.note: One LLM call plus up to two Cargo database calls (matchBusiness, enrichBusinessFirmographics) per account, on arrival and again on the weekly stale sweep (last scored 3+ months ago).
cost.scalesWith: accounts in the model, times re-scores. A TAM built by tam-building scores at that size.
